newsitem.title: UK: British Airways says plans to sell all USAir shares.
newsitem.headline: British Airways says plans to sell all USAir shares.

text.p: British Airways, which is planning a strategic alliance with U.S. carrier American Airlines, said on Wednesday it planned to sell all of its 25 percent stake in another U.S. airline, USAir.

The British airline said in a statement it was required to offer the shares to USAir before selling them and USAir has 60 days to decide whether to purchase. It said it was not disclosing the price it has offered.
BA said if USAir did not take up the offer, BA would be free to sell its stake by private transaction or by public offering.

BA said its three directors on USAir's board would resign when the stake is sold. In the statement, BA's chief executive officer Bob Ayling said the sale had not resulted from USAir's recent lawsuit against BA related to the proposed alliance with American Airlines.

"British Airways has taken this action with regret. But it has become inevitable. It would clearly be unwise to pursue an alliance with an unwilling partner. We still believe the legal action to be groundless," Ayling said.
